text:
marta: Quick ask — can someone run a short on‑prem VPC networking smoke (fio + ethtool + bench-runner) on DC1 nodes? We're seeing occasional token p95 spikes in private canary and want to rule out NIC offload / IRQ affinity differences before we sign off.

ethan: I can take this. Which AMI/kernel and which host pool? also: do you want both irqbalance and cpu-isolation runs? :eyes:

marta: AMI is `redwood-inference-onprem-2025-ami-v2` (kernel 5.15 backports). Run against pool `vpc-onprem-dc1-small`. Yes run two variants: (A) default irqbalance, (B) manual irq affinity + isolated cpus. Use bench-runner profile `net-io`. Save raw artifacts to `gs://redwood-private-bench/1992468000/`.

sre-bot: Reminder: for reproducible network runs set `isolcpus` kernel arg for isolated case OR use systemd `CPUAffinity` for the inference process. Also capture hugepages info: `grep Hugepagesize /proc/meminfo`.

zhou: On the NIC side I noticed some machines have LRO/GRO enabled by default on the driver. I'll include `ethtool -k` and disable GSO/GRO/TCP offloads for the second run: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off tso off`. I'll also collect `ethtool -S eth0` before/after.

clara: Small checklist for the run so results are comparable:
- kernel cmdline copy
- `cat /proc/interrupts`
- `lscpu`
- `sysctl net.core.default_qdisc`
- fio job used + runtime
- bench-runner args
Do both `fq` and `fq_codel` qdisc runs if possible.

ivan: I'll take the post-processing: flamegraphs for softirq/irq, and a small script to compute token-latency p50/p95/p99. ETA ~2h after runs finish. Ping me when artifacts are uploaded.

ethan: Running now (1992468123). Commands I used: 
```
# smoke fio for write/read latency
sudo fio --name=net-smoke --rw=readwrite --bs=4k --numjobs=4 --iodepth=64 --size=1G --runtime=300 --time_based
# bench-runner
bench-runner --profile net-io --target qps=1000 --seq-len=2048 --save /tmp/bench-1992468123.json
# ethtool checks
sudo ethtool -k eth0 > /tmp/ethtool-before.txt
sudo ethtool -S eth0 > /tmp/ethtool-stats.txt
```
Quick raw summary from the net-run (A: irqbalance): p50=38ms p95=112ms p99=240ms. Disk fio latencies negligible.

marta: Thanks — p95=112ms is borderline but not a hard fail. If p99 is 240ms that's a red flag for tails. Can you also run variant B (isolated cpus + offloads off) and re-run bench-runner with `--save /tmp/bench-iso.json`?

ethan: Variant B started (1992468380). I disabled offloads and pinned the inference process to cpus 4-11 using taskset. Also set `net.core.default_qdisc=fq` for this run.

ethan: Result (variant B): p50=35ms p95=78ms p99=140ms. CPU steal ~0. No obvious RX drops in ethtool. Logs + artifacts uploaded.

deploy-bot: Artifacts uploaded: gs://redwood-private-bench/1992468000/ethan/ (bench-1992468123.json, bench-iso.json, ethtool-*.txt, fio-*.log) :white_check_mark:

ivan: Downloading now. I'll produce a short diff report and flamegraphs. Main guess: offloads + affinity reduced softirq latency and improved p95. I'll post a one-paragraph note to the infra wiki and link to the artifacts.

marta: Great work. Action items: (1) Ivan: add short remediation playbook for onprem teams (kernel flags + ethtool checklist). (2) Clara: add the qdisc matrix to the parity test plan. (3) Ethan/Zhou: mark any hosts with persistent LRO and schedule driver update if needed.

clara: Will add to the parity doc. Quick: do we want to include a minimal smoke script to run these checks in `infra/bench-scripts`? Could save time for future canaries.

marta: Yes please — a one-shot script that runs `fio`, `bench-runner`, `ethtool` dumps and collects the sys info. Make it idempotent and upload to the same GCS path.

ethan: I'll PR a bash script and example systemd unit that runs pre-flight checks. Linking PR when ready. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: keep timestamps and node names in JSON artifacts for traceability (use `--meta host=$(hostname) --meta ts=$(date +%s)`).

marta: Perfect — thanks everyone. If anything weird shows up in the diff report @ivan, call it out as a regression and we'll roll back kernel param changes.
